_meta.indication: VOSEVI is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A) who have: genotype 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 infection previously treated with an HCV regimen containing an NS5A inhibitor; or genotype 1a or 3 infection previously treated with an HCV regimen containing sofosbuvir without an NS5A inhibitor.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; only genotype 1 subjects were randomized 1:1, and genotype 2-6 subjects all received VOSEVI.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic HCV genotype 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 infection, without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis, who previously failed an HCV regimen containing an NS5A inhibitor.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12 (sustained virologic response, HCV RNA less than LLOQ) measured 12 weeks after the end of therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: 415 treated (VOSEVI 12 weeks N=263; Placebo 12 weeks N=152)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall SVR12 96% (253/263) with VOSEVI; no placebo subjects achieved SVR12 (exceeded the prespecified 85% threshold).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial comparing VOSEVI vs SOF/VEL, each 12 weeks; genotype 1-3 randomized 1:1, genotype 4 received VOSEVI.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic HCV genotype 1, 2, 3, or 4 infection, without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis, who had previously failed a HCV DAA-containing regimen that did not include an NS5A inhibitor.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12 (HCV RNA less than LLOQ) measured 12 weeks after the end of therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: 333 treated (VOSEVI 12 weeks N=182; SOF/VEL 12 weeks N=151)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall 98% achieved SVR12; VOSEVI produced numerically higher SVR12 rates than SOF/VEL in genotype 3 (96% [52/54] vs 85% [44/52]); additional benefit of VOSEVI over sofosbuvir/velpatasvir was not shown in adults with genotype 1b, 2, 4, 5, or 6 infection.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=10%) were headache, fatigue, diarrhea, and nausea. In POLARIS-1: headache 21% vs 14% placebo, fatigue 17% vs 15%, diarrhea 13% vs 9%, nausea 13% vs 7%.
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of three HCV direct-acting antivirals: sofosbuvir (NS5B polymerase nucleotide analog inhibitor), velpatasvir (NS5A inhibitor), and voxilaprevir (NS3/4A protease inhibitor).
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination tablet of three small-molecule antivirals)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF HEPATITIS B VIRUS REACTIVATION IN PATIENTS COINFECTED WITH HCV AND HBV. HBV reactivation has been reported, in some cases resulting in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death.

advisory_committee.vote: This NDA was not presented at the Antimicrobial Drug Advisory Committee because SOF/VEL/VOX received breakthrough designation and the benefit/risk assessment did not appear controversial.

description.text: Expanded to include patients with severe renal impairment including end stage renal disease on dialysis for chronic HCV infection

citations.quote:
- The use of Vosevi for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus infection in patients with severe renal impairment including patients with end stage renal disease on dialysis.
- The addition of carbamazepine and rifabutin information to CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY, Table 6.
- The addition of data from Study TX-281-2030, a rat carcinogenicity study, to support labeling changes in NONCLINICAL TOXICOLOGY.

basis.text: Breakthrough designation granted February 19, 2016 for treatment of CHC due to HCV genotype 1 infection based on preliminary evidence of activity in patients with no approved therapy who previously failed an NS5A-inhibitor containing DAA regimen.

citations.quote: Breakthrough designation was granted in February 19, 2016 for the treatment of CHC due to HCV genotype 1 infection based on preliminary evidence that indicated that the fixed-dose combination demonstrated activity in patients for whom there was no approved therapy who previously failed an NS5A-inhibitor containing DAA regimen.

basis.text: Fast Track Designation for HCV GT 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 on June 12, 2015 because CHC is a serious condition and the fixed-dose combination demonstrated the potential to address an unmet medical need.

summary.text: VOSEVI received Fast Track Designation (June 12, 2015) and Breakthrough Therapy designation (February 19, 2016), and a priority review under PDUFA V; it was approved via the traditional pathway based on SVR12 in POLARIS-1 and POLARIS-4 and was not presented to an advisory committee.

Breakthrough designation was granted in February 19, 2016 for the treatment of CHC due to HCV genotype 1 infection based on preliminary evidence that indicated that the fixed-dose combination demonstrated activity in patients for whom there was no approved therapy who previously failed an NS5A-inhibitor containing DAA regimen.
